claim_text: Class weighting universally improves minority-class detection.
scientific_justification: Directly contradicted by empirical results: 6 of 9 configurations degraded or saw no improvement under weighting.
Overly broad claim; class weighting successfully rescued SwinUNETR 3D from 0% recall to 25% recall under Protocol C.

claim_text: Class weighting did not provide a universal improvement.
scientific_justification: Fully substantiated: ResNet18 and DenseNet121 exhibited lower LGG recall and lower Macro-F1 under Protocols B and C.

claim_text: The response to class weighting differed across architectures.
scientific_justification: CNN architectures experienced sensitivity degradation under weighting, whereas SwinUNETR only achieved non-zero sensitivity under minority weighting.

claim_text: Pretrained CNN architectures degraded under the tested weighting schemes, whereas SwinUNETR showed improvement under Protocol C.
scientific_justification: Exact description of empirical findings on the controlled benchmark.

claim_text: The effect of class weighting depends on architecture, initialization, and optimization behaviour.
scientific_justification: Mechanisms are strongly plausible and supported by convergence traces, but multi-seed and random vs pretrained initialization ablations were not exhaustively decoupled across all models.

claim_text: Class weighting is not a universal solution for minority-class imbalance in this setting.
scientific_justification: Definitively proven across all 9 canonical project experiments.
